decisions.context: Millions of documents arrive daily, with strongly seasonal volume. The brief gives no per-document response-time requirement.
decisions.rationale: Throughput and seasonal elasticity decide the choice; the system gives up immediate results in exchange for buffering and independently scaled workers.
consequences: Queue depth and worker capacity need monitoring.

decisions.context: Volume varies strongly over the year, so fixed inference capacity risks either peak shortfalls or idle capacity off peak.
decisions.rationale: Seasonal elasticity decides the choice; some scale-up lag and policy complexity are accepted to avoid sizing permanently for peak demand.
consequences: Scaling needs safe bounds and queue-aware signals.
Peak capacity still requires an explicit target.

decisions.decision: Track quality by model and time
decisions.context: Operators need to see when classification quality drifts. The brief does not specify the source or timeliness of quality labels.

alternatives.label: Monitor labeled outcomes by model version

chosen.label: Monitor labeled outcomes by model version

decisions.rationale: Detecting classification quality drift decides the choice; outcome measurement gives stronger evidence but sacrifices timeliness when labels arrive late.
consequences: Label collection and linkage are required.
Operators need thresholds and an alert workflow.

decisions.decision: Publish results through a shared result store
decisions.context: Several teams consume the same classifications. A shared durable interface avoids coupling inference workers to each consumer.
decisions.rationale: Multiple independent consuming teams decide the choice; durable shared access costs an additional storage component and persistence step.
consequences: A result schema and access controls are needed.
Retention and replay policies must be set.
